text:
Opening keynote at Fintech Builders Summit this morning: Helena Voss-Marchetti, founder and CEO of Larchmont Systems, on fraud detection for community banks. She has spent 20 years in payments infrastructure, sold a payments company, and sits on two bank boards, so she sees this problem from several sides.

Her claim: small banks lose more to fraud per account than large banks because they buy rules, not models.

Larchmont's customers have under $5B in assets, and most have no data-science team. Their answer is one shared model across 90 banks, trained on pooled, anonymised fraud labels. A small bank gets the benefit of patterns it would never see on its own.

The line of the morning: "A rule you can't update by Friday is a rule the fraudsters already know."

She also expects regulators to require explainable fraud decisions within two years.

My takeaway from a go-to-market seat: when your buyer has no data team, you're selling an outcome they can't build themselves, and explainability stops being a nice-to-have.

Are you seeing the same shift from rules to shared models in the banks you work with?
